verses.zh: 当那一天，耶稣从房子里出来，坐在海边。
verses.en: On that day after Jesus went out of the house, he sat by the lake.[NOTE:1]
notes: Here lake refers to the Sea of Galilee.

verses.zh: 有许多人到他那里聚集，他只得上船坐下，众人都站在岸上。
verses.en: And such a large crowd gathered around him that he got into a boat[NOTE:1] to sit while[NOTE:2] the whole crowd stood on the shore.
notes: See the note at Matt 4:21 for a description of the first-century fishing boat discovered in 1986 near Tiberias on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee.
Grk “and all the crowd.” The clause in this phrase, although coordinate in terms of grammar, is logically subordinate to the previous clause.

verses.zh: 他用比喻对他们讲许多道理，说：「有一个撒种的出去撒种；
verses.en: He[NOTE:1] told them many things in parables,[NOTE:2] saying: “Listen![NOTE:3] A sower went out to sow.[NOTE:4]
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated.

Though parables can contain a variety of figures of speech (cf. the remainder of chapter 13), many times they are simply stories that attempt to teach spiritual truth (which is unknown to the hearers) by using a comparison with something known to the hearers. In general, parables usually advance a single idea, though there may be many parts and characters in a single parable and subordinate ideas may expand the main idea further. The beauty of using the parable as a teaching device is that it draws the listener into the story, elicits an evaluation, and demands a response.
Grk “Behold.”

A sower went out to sow. The background for this well-known parable, drawn from a typical scene in the Palestinian countryside, is a field through which a well-worn path runs. Sowing would occur in late fall or early winter (October to December) in the rainy season, looking for sprouting in April or May and a June harvest. The use of seed as a figure for God’s giving life has OT roots (Isa 55:10-11). The point of the parable of the sower is to illustrate the various responses to the message of the kingdom of God.

verses.zh: 撒的时候，有落在路旁的，飞鸟来吃尽了；
verses.en: And as he sowed, some seeds[NOTE:1] fell along the path, and the birds came and devoured them.
notes: In Matthew’s version of this parable, plural pronouns are used to refer to the seed in v. 4 (ἅ…αὐτά [ha…auta]), although the collective singular is used in v. 5 and following (indicated by the singular verbs like ἔπεσεν [epesen]). For the sake of consistency in English, plural pronouns referring to the seed are used in the translation throughout the Matthean account. In both Mark and Luke the collective singular is used consistently throughout (cf. Mark 4:1-9; Luke 8:4-8).

verses.zh: 有落在土浅石头地上的，土既不深，发苗最快，
verses.en: Other[NOTE:1] seeds fell on rocky ground[NOTE:2] where they did not have much soil. They sprang up quickly because the soil was not deep.[NOTE:3]
notes: Here and in vv. 7 and 8 δέ (de) has not been translated.
The rocky ground in Palestine would be a limestone base lying right under the soil.
Grk “because it did not have depth of earth.”

verses.zh: 日头出来一晒，因为没有根，就枯干了；
verses.en: But when the sun came up, they were scorched, and because they did not have sufficient root, they withered.

verses.zh: 有落在荆棘里的，荆棘长起来，把它挤住了；
verses.en: Other seeds fell among the thorns,[NOTE:1] and they grew up and choked them.[NOTE:2]
notes: Palestinian weeds like these thorns could grow up to 6 feet in height and have a major root system.
That is, crowded out the good plants.

verses.zh: 又有落在好土里的，就结实，有一百倍的，有六十倍的，有三十倍的。
verses.en: But other seeds fell on good soil and produced grain, some a hundred times as much, some sixty, and some thirty.

verses.zh: 有耳可听的，就应当听！」
verses.en: The one who has ears had better listen!”[NOTE:1]
notes: The translation “had better listen!” captures the force of the third person imperative more effectively than the traditional “let him hear,” which sounds more like a permissive than an imperative to the modern English reader. This was Jesus’ common expression to listen and heed carefully (cf. Matt 11:15; 13:43; Mark 4:9, 23; Luke 8:8; 14:35).

verses.zh: 门徒进前来，问耶稣说：「对众人讲话，为甚么用比喻呢？」
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] the disciples came to him and said, “Why do you speak to them in parables?”
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.

verses.zh: 耶稣回答说：「因为天国的奥秘只叫你们知道，不叫他们知道。
verses.en: He replied,[NOTE:1] “You have been given[NOTE:2] the opportunity to know[NOTE:3] the secrets[NOTE:4] of the kingdom of heaven, but they have not.
notes: Grk “And answering, he said to them.” This construction is somewhat redundant in English and has been simplified in the translation. Here δέ (de) has not been translated.
This is an example of a “divine passive,” with God understood to be the source of the revelation (see ExSyn 437-38).
Grk “to you it has been given to know.” The dative pronoun occurs first, in emphatic position in the Greek text, although this position is awkward in contemporary English.

Grk “the mysteries.”sn The key term secrets (μυστήριον, mustērion) can mean either (1) a new revelation or (2) a revealing interpretation of existing revelation as in Dan 2:17-23, 27-30. Jesus seems to be explaining how current events develop old promises, since the NT consistently links the events of Jesus’ ministry and message with old promises (Rom 1:1-4; Heb 1:1-2). The traditional translation of this word, “mystery,” is misleading to the modern English reader because it suggests a secret which people have tried to uncover but which they have failed to understand (L&N 28.77).

verses.zh: 凡有的，还要加给他，叫他有余；凡没有的，连他所有的，也要夺去。
verses.en: For whoever has will be given more, and will have an abundance. But whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken from him.[NOTE:1]
notes: What he has will be taken from him. The meaning is that the one who accepts Jesus’ teaching concerning his person and the kingdom will receive a share in the kingdom now and even more in the future, but for the one who rejects Jesus’ words, the opportunity that that person presently possesses with respect to the kingdom will someday be taken away forever.

verses.zh: 所以我用比喻对他们讲，是因他们看也看不见，听也听不见，也不明白。
verses.en: For this reason I speak to them in parables: Although they see they do not see, and although they hear they do not hear nor do they understand.

verses.zh: 在他们身上，正应了以赛亚的预言，说：你们听是要听见，却不明白；看是要看见，却不晓得；
verses.en: And concerning them the prophecy of Isaiah is fulfilled that says: “‘You will listen carefully[NOTE:1] yet will never understand, you will look closely[NOTE:2] yet will never comprehend.
notes: Grk “with hearing,” a cognate dative that intensifies the action of the main verb “you will listen” (ExSyn 168-69).
Grk “look by looking.” The participle is redundant, functioning to intensify the force of the main verb.

verses.zh: 因为这百姓油蒙了心，耳朵发沉，眼睛闭着，恐怕眼睛看见，耳朵听见，心里明白，回转过来，我就医治他们。
verses.en: For the heart of this people has become dull;they are hard of hearing, and they have shut their eyes, so that they would not see with their eyes and hear with their ears and understand with their hearts and turn, and I would heal them.’[NOTE:1]
notes: A quotation from Isa 6:9-10. Thus parables both conceal or reveal depending on whether one is open to hearing what they teach.

verses.zh: 「但你们的眼睛是有福的，因为看见了；你们的耳朵也是有福的，因为听见了。
verses.en: “But your eyes are blessed[NOTE:1] because they see, and your ears because they hear.
notes: This beatitude highlights the great honor bestowed on the disciples to share in this salvation.

verses.zh: 我实在告诉你们，从前有许多先知和义人要看你们所看的，却没有看见，要听你们所听的，却没有听见。」
verses.en: For I tell you the truth,[NOTE:1] many prophets and righteous people longed to see[NOTE:2] what you see but did not see it, and to hear what you hear but did not hear it.
notes: Grk “truly (ἀμήν, amēn) I say to you.”
This is what past prophets and righteous people had wanted very much to see, yet the fulfillment had come to the disciples. This remark is like 1 Pet 1:10-12 or Heb 1:1-2.

verses.zh: 「所以，你们当听这撒种的比喻。
verses.en: “So listen to the parable of the sower:

verses.zh: 凡听见天国道理不明白的，那恶者就来，把所撒在他心里的夺了去；这就是撒在路旁的了。
verses.en: When anyone hears the word about the kingdom and does not understand it, the evil one[NOTE:1] comes and snatches what was sown in his heart;[NOTE:2] this is the seed sown along the path.
notes: Interestingly, the synoptic parallels each use a different word for Satan here: Mark 4:15 has “Satan,” while Luke 8:12 has “the devil.” This illustrates the fluidity of the gospel tradition in often using synonyms at the same point of the parallel tradition.
The word of Jesus has the potential to save if it germinates in a person’s heart, something the devil is very much against.

verses.zh: 撒在石头地上的，就是人听了道，当下欢喜领受，
verses.en: The[NOTE:1] seed sown on rocky ground[NOTE:2] is the person who hears the word and immediately receives it with joy.
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.
Grk “The one sown on rocky ground, this is the one.” The next two statements like this one have this same syntactical structure.

verses.zh: 只因心里没有根，不过是暂时的，及至为道遭了患难，或是受了逼迫，立刻就跌倒了。
verses.en: But he has no root in himself and does not endure;[NOTE:1] when[NOTE:2] trouble or persecution comes because of the word, immediately he falls away.
notes: Grk “is temporary.”
Here δέ (de) has not been translated.

verses.zh: 撒在荆棘里的，就是人听了道，后来有世上的思虑、钱财的迷惑把道挤住了，不能结实。
verses.en: The[NOTE:1] seed sown among thorns is the person who hears the word, but worldly cares and the seductiveness of wealth[NOTE:2] choke the word,[NOTE:3] so it produces nothing.
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.
Grk “the deceitfulness of riches.” Cf. BDAG 99 s.v. ἀπάτη 1, “the seduction which comes from wealth.”
That is, their concern for spiritual things is crowded out by material things.

verses.zh: 撒在好地上的，就是人听道明白了，后来结实，有一百倍的，有六十倍的，有三十倍的。」
verses.en: But as for the seed sown on good soil, this is the person who hears the word and understands. He bears fruit, yielding a hundred, sixty, or thirty times what was sown.”[NOTE:1]
notes: The Greek is difficult to translate because it switches from a generic “he” to three people within this generic class (thus, something like: “Who indeed bears fruit and yields, in one instance a hundred times, in another, sixty times, in another, thirty times”).

verses.zh: 耶稣又设个比喻对他们说：「天国好像人撒好种在田里，
verses.en: He presented them with another parable:[NOTE:1] “The kingdom of heaven is like a person who sowed good seed in his field.
notes: Grk “He set before them another parable, saying.” The participle λέγων (legōn) is redundant and has not been translated.

verses.zh: 及至人睡觉的时候，有仇敌来，将稗子撒在麦子里就走了。
verses.en: But while everyone was sleeping, an enemy came and sowed darnel[NOTE:1] among the wheat and went away.
notes: Or “sowed poisonous weeds”; KJV “tares.” The Greek term ζιζάνιον (zizanion) is generally understood to refer to darnel (Lolium temulentum), an especially undesirable weed that bears an uncanny resemblance to wheat until the ears of grain appear (L&N 3.30; BDAG 429 s.v.). So close is the resemblance to genuine wheat that darnel is sometimes called “false wheat.” Darnel is considered poisonous; ingesting the weed causes feelings of drunkenness and can prove fatal. Under Roman law the sowing of such poisonous plants in someone else’s field was specifically prohibited (C. Keener, The Gospel of Matthew: A Socio-Rhetorical Commentary [Eerdmans, 2009], 387). A number of recent English translations use “weeds,” but this does not convey the poisonous nature of darnel or the similarity in appearance to wheat.

verses.zh: 到长苗吐穗的时候，稗子也显出来。
verses.en: When[NOTE:1] the plants sprouted and produced grain, then the darnel also appeared.
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.

verses.zh: 田主的仆人来告诉他说：『主啊，你不是撒好种在田里吗？从哪里来的稗子呢？』
verses.en: So the slaves[NOTE:1] of the landowner[NOTE:2] came and said to him, ‘Sir, didn’t you sow good seed in your field? Then where did the darnel come from?’
notes: See the note on the word “slave” in 8:9.
The term landowner here refers to the owner and manager of a household.

verses.zh: 主人说：『这是仇敌做的。』仆人说：『你要我们去薅出来吗？』
verses.en: He said, ‘An enemy has done this!’ So[NOTE:1] the slaves replied, ‘Do you want us to go and gather it?’
notes: Here δέ (de) has been translated as “so” to indicate the implied result of the owner’s statement.

verses.zh: 主人说：『不必，恐怕薅稗子，连麦子也拔出来。
verses.en: But he said, ‘No, since in gathering the darnel you may uproot the wheat along with it.

verses.zh: 容这两样一齐长，等着收割。当收割的时候，我要对收割的人说，先将稗子薅出来，捆成捆，留着烧；惟有麦子要收在仓里。』」
verses.en: Let both grow together until the harvest. At[NOTE:1] harvest time I will tell the reapers, “First collect the darnel and tie it in bundles to be burned, but then gather[NOTE:2] the wheat into my barn.”’”
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated.
Grk “burned, but gather”; “then” has been added to the English translation to complete the sequence begun by “First collect.”

verses.zh: 他又设个比喻对他们说：「天国好像一粒芥菜种，有人拿去种在田里。
verses.en: He gave[NOTE:1] them another parable:[NOTE:2] “The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed[NOTE:3] that a man took and sowed in his field.
notes: Grk “put before.”
Grk “He set before them another parable, saying.” The participle λέγων (legōn) is redundant and has not been translated.
The mustard seed was noted for its tiny size.

verses.zh: 这原是百种里最小的，等到长起来，却比各样的菜都大，且成了树，天上的飞鸟来宿在它的枝上。」
verses.en: It is the smallest of all the seeds, but when it has grown it is the greatest garden plant and becomes a tree,[NOTE:1] so that the wild birds[NOTE:2] come and nest in its branches.”[NOTE:3]
notes: This is rhetorical hyperbole, since technically a mustard plant is not a tree. This could refer to one of two types of mustard plant popular in Palestine and would be either ten or twenty-five ft (3 or 7.5 m) tall.

Grk “the birds of the sky” or “the birds of the heaven”; the Greek word οὐρανός (ouranos) may be translated either “sky” or “heaven,” depending on the context. The idiomatic expression “birds of the sky” refers to wild birds as opposed to domesticated fowl (cf. BDAG 809 s.v. πετεινόν).

The point of the parable seems to be that while the kingdom of God may appear to have insignificant and unnoticeable beginnings (i.e., in the ministry of Jesus), it will someday (i.e., at the second advent) be great and quite expansive. The kingdom, however, is not to be equated with the church, but rather the church is an expression of the kingdom. Also, there is important OT background in the image of a small plant that grew and became a tree: Ezek 17:22-24 pictures the reemergence of the Davidic house where people can find calm and shelter. Like the mustard seed, it would start out small but grow to significant size.

verses.zh: 他又对他们讲个比喻说：「天国好像面酵，有妇人拿来，藏在三斗面里，直等全团都发起来。」
verses.en: He told them another parable: “The kingdom of heaven is like yeast that a woman took and mixed with[NOTE:1] three measures[NOTE:2] of flour until all the dough had risen.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “hid in.”

This measure was a saton, the Greek name for the Hebrew term “seah.” Three of these was a very large quantity of flour, since a saton is a little over 16 pounds (7 kg) of dry measure (or 13.13 liters). So this was over 47 lbs (21 kg) of flour total, enough to feed over a hundred people.

Grk “it was all leavened.”sn The parable of the yeast and the dough teaches that the kingdom of God will start small but eventually grow to permeate everything. Jesus’ point was not to be deceived by its seemingly small start, the same point made in the parable of the mustard seed, which preceded this one.

verses.zh: 这都是耶稣用比喻对众人说的话；若不用比喻，就不对他们说甚么。
verses.en: Jesus spoke all these things in parables to the crowds; he did not speak to them without a parable.

verses.zh: 这是要应验先知的话，说：我要开口用比喻，把创世以来所隐藏的事发明出来。
verses.en: This fulfilled what was spoken by the prophet:[NOTE:1] “I will open my mouth in parables, I will announce what has been hidden from the foundation of the world.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “was spoken by the prophet, saying.” The participle λέγοντος (legontos) is redundant in contemporary English and has not been translated.tc A few significant mss (א* Θ ƒ1, 13 33) identify the prophet as Isaiah, a reading that is significantly harder than the generic “prophet” because the source of this prophecy is not Isaiah but Asaph in Ps 78. Jerome mentioned some mss that had “Asaph” here, though none are known to exist today. This problem is difficult because of the temptation for scribes to delete the reference to Isaiah in order to clear up a discrepancy. Indeed, the vast majority of witnesses have only “the prophet” here (א1 B C D L W Γ Δ 0233 0242 565 579 700 1241 1424 M lat sy co). However, as B. M. Metzger points out, “if no prophet were originally named, more than one scribe might have been prompted to insert the name of the best known prophet—something which has, in fact, happened elsewhere more than once” (TCGNT 27). In light of the paucity of evidence for the reading ᾿Ησαΐου, as well as the proclivity of scribes to add his name, it is probably best to consider the shorter reading as authentic.
A quotation from Ps 78:2.

verses.zh: 当下，耶稣离开众人，进了房子。他的门徒进前来，说：「请把田间稗子的比喻讲给我们听。」
verses.en: Then he left the crowds and went into the house. And his disciples came to him saying, “Explain to us the parable of the darnel[NOTE:1] in the field.”
notes: Or “poisonous weeds.” See the note on the word “darnel” in 13:25.

verses.zh: 他回答说：「那撒好种的就是人子；
verses.en: He[NOTE:1] answered, “The one who sowed the good seed is the Son of Man.
notes: Grk “And answering, he said.” This construction is somewhat redundant in English and has been simplified in the translation. Here δέ (de) has not been translated.

verses.zh: 田地就是世界；好种就是天国之子；稗子就是那恶者之子；
verses.en: The field is the world and the good seed are the people[NOTE:1] of the kingdom. The poisonous weeds[NOTE:2] are the people[NOTE:3] of the evil one,
notes: Grk “the sons of the kingdom.” This idiom refers to people who should properly be, or were traditionally regarded as, a part of God’s kingdom. L&N 11.13 translates the phrase: “people of God’s kingdom, God’s people.”
Or “The darnels.” Here “poisonous weeds” contrasts with “the good seed” mentioned previously in the verse.
Grk “the sons of the evil one.” See the preceding note on the phrase “people of the kingdom” earlier in this verse, which is the opposite of this phrase. See also L&N 9.4; 11.13; 11.14.

verses.zh: 撒稗子的仇敌就是魔鬼；收割的时候就是世界的末了；收割的人就是天使。
verses.en: and the enemy who sows them is the devil. The harvest is the end of the age, and the reapers are angels.

verses.zh: 将稗子薅出来用火焚烧，世界的末了也要如此。
verses.en: As[NOTE:1] the poisonous weeds[NOTE:2] are collected and burned with fire, so it will be at the end of the age.
notes: Grk “Therefore as.” Here οὖν (oun) has not been translated.
Or “the darnels.”

verses.zh: 人子要差遣使者，把一切叫人跌倒的和作恶的，从他国里挑出来，
verses.en: The Son of Man will send his angels, and they will gather from his kingdom everything that causes sin as well as all lawbreakers.[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “the ones who practice lawlessness.”

verses.zh: 丢在火炉里；在那里必要哀哭切齿了。
verses.en: They will throw them into the fiery furnace,[NOTE:1] where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
notes: A quotation from Dan 3:6.

verses.zh: 那时，义人在他们父的国里，要发出光来，像太阳一样。有耳可听的，就应当听！」
verses.en: Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father.[NOTE:1] The one who has ears had better listen![NOTE:2]
notes: An allusion to Dan 12:3.

The translation “had better listen!” captures the force of the third person imperative more effectively than the traditional “let him hear,” which sounds more like a permissive than an imperative to the modern English reader. This was Jesus’ common expression to listen and heed carefully (cf. Matt 11:15; 13:9; Mark 4:9, 23; Luke 8:8; 14:35).

verses.zh: 「天国好像宝贝藏在地里，人遇见了就把它藏起来，欢欢喜喜地去变卖一切所有的，买这块地。
verses.en: “The kingdom of heaven is like a treasure, hidden in a field, that a person found and hid. Then because of joy he went and sold all that he had and bought that field.

verses.zh: 天国又好像买卖人寻找好珠子，
verses.en: “Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a merchant searching for fine pearls.

verses.zh: 遇见一颗重价的珠子，就去变卖他一切所有的，买了这颗珠子。
verses.en: When he found a pearl of great value, he went out and sold everything he had and bought it.

verses.zh: 天国又好像网撒在海里，聚拢各样水族，
verses.en: “Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a net that was cast into the sea that caught all kinds of fish.

verses.zh: 网既满了，人就拉上岸来，坐下，拣好的收在器具里，将不好的丢弃了。
verses.en: When it was full, they pulled it ashore, sat down, and put the good fish into containers and threw the bad away.

verses.zh: 世界的末了也要这样。天使要出来，从义人中把恶人分别出来，
verses.en: It will be this way at the end of the age. Angels will come and separate the evil from the righteous

verses.zh: 丢在火炉里；在那里必要哀哭切齿了。」
verses.en: and throw them into the fiery furnace,[NOTE:1] where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
notes: An allusion to Dan 3:6.

verses.zh: 耶稣说：「这一切的话你们都明白了吗？」他们说：「我们明白了。」
verses.en: “Have you understood all these things?” They replied, “Yes.”

verses.zh: 他说：「凡文士受教作天国的门徒，就像一个家主从他库里拿出新旧的东西来。」
verses.en: Then he said to them, “Therefore every expert in the law[NOTE:1] who has been trained for the kingdom of heaven is like the owner of a house who brings out of his treasure what is new and old.”
notes: Or “every scribe.” See the note on the phrase “experts in the law” in 2:4. It is possible that the term translated “expert in the law” (traditionally, “scribe”) here is a self-description used by the author, Matthew, to represent his role in conveying the traditions about Jesus to his intended audience. See David E. Orton, The Understanding Scribe [JSNTSup].

verses.zh: 耶稣说完了这些比喻，就离开那里，
verses.en: Now when[NOTE:1] Jesus finished these parables, he moved on from there.
notes: Grk “Now it happened that when.” The introductory phrase καὶ ἐγένετο (kai egeneto, “it happened that”) is redundant in contemporary English and has not been translated.

verses.zh: 来到自己的家乡，在会堂里教训人，甚至他们都希奇，说：「这人从哪里有这等智慧和异能呢？
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] he came to his hometown[NOTE:2] and began to teach the people[NOTE:3] in their synagogue.[NOTE:4] They[NOTE:5] were astonished and said, “Where did this man get such wisdom and miraculous powers?
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “Then.”
Jesus’ hometown (where he spent his childhood years) was Nazareth, about 20 miles (30 km) southwest of Capernaum.
Grk “them”; the referent (the people) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
See the note on synagogues in 4:23. Jesus undoubtedly took the opportunity on this occasion to speak about his person and mission, and the relation of both to OT fulfillment.
Grk “synagogue, so that they.” Here ὥστε (hōste) has not been translated. Instead a new sentence was started in the translation.

verses.zh: 这不是木匠的儿子吗？他母亲不是叫马利亚吗？他弟兄们不是叫雅各、约西（有古卷：约瑟）、西门、犹大吗？
verses.en: Isn’t this the carpenter’s son? Isn’t his mother named Mary?[NOTE:1] And aren’t his brothers James, Joseph, Simon, and Judas?
notes: The reference to Jesus as the carpenter’s son is probably derogatory, indicating that they knew Jesus only as a common laborer like themselves. The reference to his mother…Mary (even though Jesus’ father was probably dead by this point) appears to be somewhat derogatory, for a man was not regarded as his mother’s son in Jewish usage unless an insult was intended (cf. Judg 11:1-2; John 6:42; 8:41; 9:29).

verses.zh: 他妹妹们不是都在我们这里吗？这人从哪里有这一切的事呢？」
verses.en: And aren’t all his sisters here with us? So where did he get all this?”

verses.zh: 他们就厌弃他（厌弃他：原文是因他跌倒）。耶稣对他们说：「大凡先知，除了本地本家之外，没有不被人尊敬的。」
verses.en: And so they took offense at him. But Jesus said to them, “A prophet is not without honor except in his hometown and in his own house.”

verses.zh: 耶稣因为他们不信，就在那里不多行异能了。
verses.en: And he did not do many miracles there because of their unbelief.
